sections.title: Phases of VKH Syndrome
content: 1. Prodromal Phase: Neurological & Auditory manifestations, Cranial nerve palsies, Optic neuritis.

2. Acute Uveitic Phase: Bilateral granulomatous AU, Multifocal posterior uveitis, Diffuse choroidal infiltrate, Dalen-Fuchs nodules, Vitritis, Papillitis, Exudative retinal detachments, Ciliary effusion, Iris lens diaphragm rotation.
3. Convalescent Phase: Development of integumentary signs (Alopecia, Poliosis, Vitiligo, Sunset glow fundus).
4. Chronic Recurrent Phase: Smouldering anterior uveitis with exacerbations, recurrent posterior uveitis.

sections.title: Modified Diagnostic Criteria for VKH
content: 1. Absence of history of penetrating ocular trauma
2. Absence of other ocular diseases and entities
3. Bilateral uveitis
4. Neurological, auditory manifestations
5. Integumentary: Localized alopecia, poliosis, vitiligo, depigmented fundus (sunset glow), depigmented limbal lesions (Sugiura sign) in pigmented Japanese patients

sections.title: Advanced VKH Investigations
content: LP (Lumbar Puncture): Lymphocytic pleocytosis, melanin-containing macrophages
FAF: Hyperautofluorescence in areas of serous detachment
U/S: Diffuse choroidal thickness; use to exclude posterior scleritis
FA: Multifocal hyperfluorescent dots (RPE level); Chronic phase shows RPE window defect
OCT: Used to quantify subretinal fluid
ICGA: Monitoring acute phase; regularly distributed hypofluorescent spots (most remain hypo in late phase); diffuse hyperfluorescence over posterior pole

sections.title: Investigations for Sarcoidosis
content: 1. Negative tuberculin skin test
2. Elevated ACE levels +/- elevated serum lysozyme
3. Chest X-ray: Bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy (BHL)
4. Chest High Resolution CT (HRCT) scan
5. Fiberoptic bronchoscopy with biopsy
6. Thoracic endosonography
7. Biopsy sites: Lymph node, skin lesion, conjunctival nodules, lacrimal gland, vitreous biopsy (CD4/CD8 ratio)
8. MRI cardiac and CNS imaging, PET scan, whole body Gallium scan
9. Calcium, Vit D levels
10. Hypercalciuria
11. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL): CD4/CD8 T-cell ratio is key indicator
12. Induced sputum analysis

sections.title: IWOS Diagnostic Levels for Ocular Sarcoidosis

rows: Chest X-ray shows bihilar lymphadenopathy + compatible uveitis
> 3/7 of intraocular signs + > 2/5 positive lab tests

sections.title: Behcet Disease Diagnostic Criteria
content: Recurrent oral ulceration (3 times in 12m) - MANDATORY
PLUS 2 OF THE FOLLOWING:
Genital ulceration
Ocular inflammation
Skin lesions (Erythema nodosum, pseudofolliculitis, acneform nodules, papulopustular lesions)
Positive Pathergy reaction (Pustule 24-48h after sterile needle prick) - >95% specific

sections.title: Systemic Manifestations of Behcet's
content: Vascular: Aneurysm (pulmonary, coronary), venous thrombosis, thrombophlebitis
Arthritis: 30% arthralgia
Neurological: 5% meningoencephalocele of brainstem, dural sinus thrombosis, cerebral aneurysm
GIT: Ileocecal involvement
Hepatic & Renal: Relatively uncommon

sections.title: Ocular Behcet: Clinical Presentation
content: 1. Acute Anterior Uveitis: 'White eye', shifting hypopyon, non-granulomatous uveitis
2. Vitritis
3. Retinitis: Transient superficial white infiltrates (heal without scarring), deeper diffuse retinitis, exudative detachment, inflammatory deposits (KP-like) on inferior peripheral retina
4. Retinal Vasculitis: Artery and vein sheathing, perivascular hemorrhage, occlusion, CMO, diffuse retinal edema
5. Optic Disc: Hyperemia and edema (due to increased ICP), leading to optic atrophy
6. Other: Conjunctival ulcers, episcleritis, scleritis, ophthalmoplegia (from neuro involvement)

sections.title: End Stage Disease in Behcet
content: Optic atrophy
Retinal atrophy
Gliosis and sheathing
Attenuation and ghosting of affected vessels
Posterior synechia, Cataract, Glaucoma
Retinal detachment
Phthisis bulbi

sections.title: Behcet's: Investigations
content: HLA-B51 Association
Pathergy Test
ESR, CRP, WBC, Complement levels
Thrombophilia screening
Fluorescein Angiography (FA): Delineate ischemia, detect inflammation, monitor activity
Laser Flare Photometry: Correlate AC activity with inflammation levels
Biopsy: Superficial lesions, synovial fluid aspiration, lumbar puncture
Imaging: MRI, MRA, CT, CTA (identify ischemia)

sections.title: Behcet Disease Management Protocol
content: 1. Immunomodulatory therapy: The mainstay of treatment
2. Topical Steroids: Alone effective only if NO posterior segment involvement
3. Initial Management: Systemic steroids + Azathioprine (2.5mg/kg)
4. Severe Disease: Cyclosporine (2-5mg/kg) OR Infliximab + Azathioprine + Steroids
5. Posterior Uveitis: Single Infliximab infusion as initial treatment
6. TB Precaution: Infliximab may activate T.B; must give with Isoniazid if risk present
7. Vision Threatening: Infliximab or Adalimumab for early vision-threatening BD
8. Intravitreal Administration: Infliximab as an option
9. Interferon Alfa: 6 million IU per day subcutaneously

rows: Xanthelasma (cholestasis, primary biliary cirrhosis), Epicanthic fold (Zellweger syndrome)
